Topic 12.1: Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of Strand 12 in Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should you speak at the right speed? 2. How can one pass a message without using words?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. say words containing the sounds /ʌ/ /ɔː/ and the consonant clusters ‘br’ ‘sw’ ‘pr’ ‘cl’ ‘gr’ correctly,
2. select words with the sounds /ʌ/ /ɔː/ and the consonant clusters ‘br’ ‘sw’ ‘pr’ ‘cl’ ‘gr’ from an oral text,
3. construct sentences that require a yes or no response using the vocabulary,
4. repeat oral texts from the teacher or an audio recording without hesitations,
5. make short speeches on the environment accurately, at the right speed and with expression, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This iss achieved as the learner makes short speeches in collaboration with peers.

• Creativity and Imagination: The learner creatively composes a speech on clean environment and delivers it fluently to

the peers.

Values:
Respect is nurtured as the learner respects the peers’ opinions when reciting poems collaboratively.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social Cohesion and integrity are enhanced as the learner engages with peers in doing activities such as reciting poems and

making short speeches.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to link fluency in speaking to all learning areas as fluency is required when making presentations.
